# Description

Certain output variables don't have similar results between the QNMs and the MSEs. Run sensitivity analyses for the following variables in the specific QNMs:


Fishery 1 - all. aggregate results separately for QNMs that did / didn't match the MSE direction. 

Total Catch - all. aggregate results separately for QNMs that did / didn't match the MSE direction. 

Fishery 2 & spawning biomass - Start with 2-C and 5-A, where both were mismatched.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(magrittr)
library(ggplot2)
library(QPress)
library(janitor)
library(kableExtra)

## custom functions
source(here('R/fxns/prepare.dia.R'))
source(here('R/fxns/impact.ss.R'))
source(here('R/fxns/qnm.sensitivity.R'))

## let's time things
end.timer <- function(s){round(Sys.time()-s,2)}

## read in which version of the data from qpress?
sim.date <- '20240920' ## 9/20/2024 and 9/19/2024 are the same, just run on different computers

```


## Data

Read in qnms and the output from perturbations
`system.simulate` output should have been saved as lists from qnm_mse_master.R
```{r load_models}
s <- Sys.time()


##### 0. A baseline scenario #####
m0list <- list(
  m <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_00-constantF',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],  # no constraints
  m.b <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_00B-rm-small-mesh',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],  # no constraints
  m.c <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_00C-rm-small-mesh-redistribute-small',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],  # no constraints
  m.e <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_00E-rm-inshore-small-mesh',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]]  # no constraints
)

#### 2. Effort scales according to the Thorson effort model (Thorson et al., 2013) ####
m2list <- list(
  m2 <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_2-thorsonF',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],  # no constraints
  m2.b <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_2B-rm-small-mesh',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]] , # no constraints
  m2.c <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_2C-rm-small-mesh-redistribute-small',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]] , # no constraints
  m2.d <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_2E-rm-inshore-small-mesh',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]] # no constraints
)

#### 3. Climate reduces productivity ####
m3list <- m0list

#### 4. Animals move into the “far offshore” area ####
m4list <- list(
  m4 <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_004-movement-to-inaccessible',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],  # no constraints
  m4.b <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_004B-rm-small-mesh',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],  # no constraints
  m4.c <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_004C-rm-small-mesh-redistribute-small',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],
  m4.d <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_004E-rm-inshore-small-mesh',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]]
)

#### 5. Climate increases growth rate ####
m5list <- list(
  m <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_005-growth-perturb',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],  # no constraints
  m.b <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_005B-rm-small-mesh',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],
  m.c <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_005C-rm-small-mesh-redistribute-small',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]],
  m.d <- prepare.dia(dia_name='MSE-QNM_2023-Oct_005E-rm-inshore-small-mesh',dia_path=here('data','qnm_models'))[[1]]  # no constraints
)


end.timer(s)
```

```{r load_sims}

```


## Linkage influence: Total catch

Use boosted regression trees to examine the relative importance of model edges (linkages) in determining the response of a given well-being variable to a HAB simulation in the Status Quo model based on Melbourne-Thomas et al. (2012): https://esapubs.org/archive/mono/M082/019/tree.r


### Fishery 1 catch
First, create a list object to save influence dataframes
```{r}
fish1.list <- list()
```


Use a custom function to produce two matrices: (1) the perturbation response (+1/-1/0) of each variable (column) in each simulation iteration (row); and (2) the randomly simulated weight of each edge (column) in each simulation iteration (row). Bind them together.
```{r, message=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
temp <- impact.ss(sim=cft.HABhi.sim,perturb=c("HAB"=1),monitor=NA)
temp2 <- cbind(temp[[1]],temp[[2]])
write_csv(temp2, here('omf-paper-1','data','HAB_sim_out','sensitivity','gbmIn_perturbmat_StatusQuoHAB.csv'))
```
```{r echo=FALSE}
temp2 <- read_csv(here('omf-paper-1','data','HAB_sim_out','sensitivity','gbmIn_perturbmat_StatusQuoHAB.csv'))
```

Test: Fit classification tree model with the variable *Emotional & mental health* as the response, for the Status Quo. 
```{r}
d <- cbind(temp2[,"Emotional & mental health"],temp2[,42:161])
fit3 <- gbm.step(data=d,gbm.x=2:121,gbm.y=1,family="gaussian",tree.complexity=5, learning.rate = 0.01,bag.fraction = 0.5)

saveRDS(fit3,file=here('omf-paper-1','data','HAB_sim_out','sensitivity','gbm_emotional-and-mental-health_StatusQuoHAB.rds'))
```
